title: Capacity Evidence Harness and Customer Acceptance Checklist
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a reproducible, auditable harness and methodology to produce 'capacity evidence' for Dedicated customers. This ticket scopes the benchmark harness, instrumentation, customer-facing acceptance checklist, and a defensible pass/fail gating strategy for throughput guarantees and autoscaling behavior across fleet controls.
test_plan: Design harness that can run tenant-aware traffic mixes against QA and staging Dedicated pools
Implement configurable traffic generator (ramp, sustain, burst) with KV-cache priming and prefix caching options
Integrate tracing and token-level telemetry to capture per-request tail latency and per-second token throughput
Define chronicler job that replays production-like tails using stored traffic fingerprints
Provide reproducible artifact (JSON run descriptor + seed) for each customer acceptance run
Automate result ingestion into Console dashboards and exportable report for customer signoff
test_profiles: Small-RT: 1-3 concurrent streams, median seq=64, 95th latency target low - used for latency-sensitive customers
Enterprise-Steady: 1000 concurrent short conversations, mixed seq=32-128, sustained throughput for reserved pools
Tenant-Mix: 10 tenants with heavy skew (1 tenant 40% RT, others 6% each) to validate fairness and QoS
Microburst: sudden 5x request spike for 30s to validate autoscaler and global fleet fallback
Long-Context: sustained generation with seq=2048 and KV cache hits to validate memory and kernel selection
acceptance_criteria: Sustained throughput meets committed tokens/sec ±5% for 30-minute steady window on Dedicated pool
95th percentile tail latency at or below SLA target for chosen profile (profile-specific thresholds) during sustain
Autoscaler reacts within configured policy window and scales without request errors under the Microburst profile
No customer-facing errors introduced by fallback routing or model-variant substitution during capacity saturation
Run artifacts (playbook, seed, logs, dashboards) uploaded to the customer folder and signed off by Solutions Engineer
Reproducibility: rerun with identical descriptor yields results within statistical margin for key metrics
results_summary: Initial harness prototype validated Enterprise-Steady and Microburst profiles against staging pool. Sustained TPS within -3% of expected for 20-minute window; however autoscaler latency exceeded the configured policy window by ~18s in one Microburst run and caused transient 500 errors for <0.5% of requests. Next actions: tune scale policy (cooldown and step sizes), harden retry middleware, add backpressure gating for saturation scenarios.
